text:
Stimulant medication is associated with better attention and working memory. Its effect on emotion regulation appears smaller than its effect on attention, and it does not reduce the demands stress brings. When things start slipping, rising stress is worth exploring. Asking what has changed in the load can point to other levers, such as adjusting demands and building skills. Any medication change is a conversation with the prescriber.

Where the evidence stops:
• Findings on medication and emotion regulation are limited.

Key sources:
• Isfandnia et al., 2024: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2024.105703
• Lenzi et al., 2018: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2017.08.010
